subject.title: [Bug] Session flush blocks write tool completely during compaction

question: Should silent memory-triggered compaction runs be allowed to write unrelated non-memory workspace files through the normal write tool, or must they remain limited to the configured memory file?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the repair changes the write authority of a silent housekeeping run and needs maintainer-owned security/product intent before automation changes it.

options.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
options.body: Permit writes outside the memory directory to delegate to the existing write tool while still blocking other memory files, with focused tests and docs for the boundary.

options.title: Keep the hard single-file guard
options.body: Preserve the current security boundary and document that users must wait, disable memory flush, or rerun edits after compaction when this state is active.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in override
options.body: Keep the default strict guard but add a documented operator-controlled bypass or session override if maintainers want the safer rollout path.

recommendation.title: Allow narrow non-memory passthrough
recommendation.body: Permit writes outside the memory directory to delegate to the existing write tool while still blocking other memory files, with focused tests and docs for the boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is mostly about memory-flush product/security boundaries, and steipete introduced the feature and docs that define the expected behavior.
